children: A Document is Barkpark's single content primitive — every post, page, paper, and even task is just a Document of some Schema.

In Barkpark there is no special row for a blog post versus a page versus a task. Each is a type:X row in Postgres carrying a title, a status, and a stable doc_id. A task is simply a type:task Document — which is why the Tasks plugin needs no bespoke storage, and why bp task commands are really Document mutations under the hood. This collapse to one primitive is what keeps the Content Model small and the Fresh Install Invariant honest.

A Document's structure is governed by its Schema, whose field types come from Schema v2. Scalar fields hold plain values; a Reference Field points one Document at another. Long-form body content is a PortableDoc block tree rather than raw HTML, so the same Document renders through pdrender in the terminal, through Bulldocs on the web, and through LiveView Studio for editing.

in the Content Graph. Its Reference Field values are mined by the Edge Extractor into edges, so the graph topology is nothing more than Documents and the references between them. A Document lives inside a Dataset and is scoped by Workspace + Project tenancy; its visibility depends on the active Perspective (published vs drafts). Studio, the Go TUI, and Search Facets all read the same Document rows — there is exactly one source of truth.

Documents are written through a mutation and queried over the HTTP API v1 — served by the Phoenix API and self-described to clients via the Capabilities Manifest, which is how the bp CLI knows how to list and fetch them. The Web Demo reads them through the Surfaces layer, Search ranks them as result rows, and the Graph View paints each one as a node — every surface looking at the same Document.
